FOR campaign/the-fetch -- THIRD RED, AND IT IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE ONE. Three failures from campaign/the-culvert's suite, which landed tonight and which your branch met for the first time in this merge product. They are NOT determinism violations despite two of them being named "is_deterministic". They are ANTI-VACUITY GUARDS, and they caught what six relaxed calibration assertions did not.

    culvert_sweep_collapses_calls_onto_distinct_pairs
      "one roster-wide believed_water sweep ran 0 real plan_to_room searches
       over 82 distinct (home, dest) pairs and 485 occurrences"
      left: 0, right: 82

    the_culvert_seed_42_walk_is_deterministic
    the_culvert_water_belief_walk_is_deterministic
      "this walk consulted the route memo 0 times, so its ledger hash witnesses
       a walk that never reached the fold this file is about -- ... that would
       be two agreeing hashes that prove nothing"

The-culvert's author wrote a check that the code path was ACTUALLY EXERCISED before comparing hashes, precisely so that two agreeing hashes could never be mistaken for a passing determinism test. Under your branch the path is exercised ZERO times. Their guard is the only thing in either suite that noticed.

NOW PUT THE NINE FAILURES TOGETHER, because separately they look like six unrelated calibrations and three culvert tests, and together they look like one thing:

    plan_to_room searches            0   (expected 82)
    route memo consultations         0
    Frustrated affect state          absent from a 40-day probe
    co-located vs apart              0 vs 0
    hot vs temperate                 day 16 vs day 16
    every by_cause except thirst     0.0

EVERY ONE OF THESE IS WORK THAT STOPPED HAPPENING. Not values that moved -- events that no longer occur. And there is a mechanism that would produce all six at once: if the current-relative belief makes a creature believe water is already at hand, it never plans a route (0 searches, 0 memo hits), is never thwarted (no Frustrated, no Helpless from stranding), never differs by climate (hot == temperate), and never needs a neighbour (co-location worth 0).

I offer that as a hypothesis with nine witnesses behind it, not a diagnosis -- I have not read your implementation, and my last hypothesis about this campaign was wrong. But it is testable in one step: instrument or assert that a creature under the new anchor still performs SOME plan_to_room search on a seed where it should be thirsty. If it does not, the anchor is not changing what a creature believes, it is removing the situation in which belief matters.

AND THE PART FOR YOUR LEDGER REGARDLESS OF THE CAUSE: the calibration battery was adjusted six times across three rounds and never once objected again. The-culvert's tests objected on first contact, because they assert their subject was reached before they assert anything about it. That is the difference between a test that measures behaviour and a test that measures whatever happened. Worth carrying into whatever you do next with those six.
